system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Multipolarity: Wars, Markets and Tech Rivalry
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where overlapping regional wars (Middle East, Ukraine) and political volatility (elections and populist upheavals) are driving energy and commodity shocks, amplifying market volatility and straining policy space. At the same time a strategic contest among major powers—principally the United States, China and Russia—plays out across trade controls, critical‑minerals and technology governance, and diplomatic outreach to peripheral regions. Central banks and financial markets are oscillating between inflation risks and growth worries, creating feedback loops that interact with supply‑chain stresses, cyber incidents and shifting regional security alignments.
system_description.scope: Interstate diplomacy and rivalry, regional armed conflicts and ceasefires, global energy and commodity flows, international financial markets and central‑bank policy, technology export controls and supply chains, multinational institutions, transnational non‑state actors (insurgents, proxies, hackers), and domestic political contests that reshape foreign policy.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑economic‑ecological system (the Anthropocene) — global human civilization interacting with Earth's resource limits, climate dynamics and transnational economic networks.
adjacent_subsystems: Global technology and supply‑chain and critical‑minerals governance

variables.name: Middle East regional escalation
variables.description: A widening regional conflict involving Iran, Israel, the United States, Gulf states and Houthi forces that is shifting from localized strikes into broader diplomatic mediation and disruptions to energy and maritime routes.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and revisionism
variables.description: Russia's prolonged military campaign against Ukraine, together with cross‑border sabotage and strikes, is altering frontline control, driving sustained material and political support from NATO partners and prompting Moscow's strategic outreach beyond Europe.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: Intensifying strategic competition between the United States (and allied partners) and China over export controls, AI and semiconductor technologies, supply chains and critical minerals is reshaping industrial policy, trade rules and technology governance.

variables.name: Global monetary and market stress
variables.description: Central banks (notably the Fed, ECB and BoJ) are recalibrating interest‑rate paths amid persistent inflation, rising bond yields and market volatility, forcing a repricing of global capital, fiscal pressures and investor risk premia.

variables.name: Security alignment and defense reconfiguration
variables.description: Major democracies and regional powers (the US, EU members, UK, Japan, South Korea and others) are reallocating defense spending, deepening bilateral security ties and creating new partnership architectures in response to multiple concurrent threats.
